decision.summary: The Federal Reserve voted to keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged at a range of 0 to 1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January suggests that economic growth has moderated somewhat.
changes.explanation: The Fed adjusted its view of the economy from solid growth to a moderate slowdown.

changes.quote: Consistent with its previous statement, the Committee judges that an increase in the target range for the federal funds rate remains unlikely at the April FOMC meeting.
changes.explanation: The Fed explicitly stated it will not raise rates at the next meeting in April.

changes.quote: The Committee anticipates that it will be appropriate to raise the target range for the federal funds rate when it has seen further improvement in the labor market and is reasonably confident that inflation will move back to its 2 percent objective over the medium term.
changes.explanation: The Fed removed the word 'patient' and replaced it with a condition to see further job market progress and confidence in reaching 2 percent inflation before hiking.

changes.quote: This change in the forward guidance does not indicate that the Committee has decided on the timing of the initial increase in the target range.
changes.explanation: The Fed clarified that changing its statement wording does not mean a rate hike has been scheduled for a specific date.

tone_quotes.quote: To support continued progress toward maximum employment and price stability, the Committee today reaffirmed its view that the current 0 to 1/4 percent target range for the federal funds rate remains appropriate.
Consistent with its previous statement, the Committee judges that an increase in the target range for the federal funds rate remains unlikely at the April FOMC meeting.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 11.99% APR costs about $49.96 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.93% and moved -13 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.75% would fall by about $22.04 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 5.5%, and employers added an average of 246k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was -0.1% over the past year (February 2015); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.3%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -13 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.16% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed will evaluate incoming data meeting by meeting without a fixed timetable for rate hikes. Educational forecast models suggest the next meeting has an 86 percent chance of a hold, a 4 percent chance of a cut, and a 10 percent chance of a hike.
